Andre — thanks for the clear asks and the RFP extract. Below is a concise set of options that map to common procurement patterns for Private deployments. I kept the tradeoffs explicit so your finance/procurement team can plug numbers into the SOW.

Option A — Pilot-first (minimal risk)
- Term: 6 months total (2 month pilot + 4 month staged run)
- Commit: nominal (1–3 node reserved baseline) with right-to-expand
- Starter credit: 2 months platform fee waived for pilot period if customer agrees to convert to a 12-month committed term after pilot
- Support: Standard (business hours) during pilot, upgrade to Pro (24x7 P1) on conversion
- Platform fee treatment: credit applied up-front; remaining platform fee amortized across 12-month committed term upon conversion

Option B — Accelerated commit (balanced economics)
- Term: 12–18 months
- Commit: tiered capacity (baseline + burst pool) with defined breakpoints at month 6 and 12
- Starter credit: 1 month platform fee + implementation credit (one-time) if signed within 30 days
- Support: Pro by default; add on an implementation retainer for first 3 months
- Platform fee treatment: option to amortize annually for accounting (we can provide an invoice schedule that smooths the platform fee monthly)

Operational/practical notes:
- SOC2: we can provide our attestation and a SOC2 summary within 5 business days; full report available under NDA.
- Escalation: we recommend a named escalation path with an SLO for regressions (response targets + on-call engineer for week 1 of pilot).
- Exit / downgrade: prorated credits on reserved capacity if termination after 6 months, subject to minimum usage thresholds.

I attached a starter pricing matrix (spreadsheet) with sample breakpoints and the platform fee amortization schedule you can hand to your FP&A team.

If either option looks promising, Marissa (cc'd) can publish a tailored quote and a draft SOW. Happy to hop on a 30 min call this week to align procurement and legal.

Best,
